subject: general
question: What legal document allowed Princely States to join either India or Pakistan after independence?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Instrument of Accession**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Instrument of Accession** was a legal document introduced by the British Government to allow princely states to join either India or Pakistan after independence in 1947.
 
• Under the provisions of the **Indian Independence Act of 1947**, princely states were given the choice to accede to either of the two dominions or remain independent.
 
• The Instrument of Accession granted the dominion (India or Pakistan) control over specific subjects like defense, foreign affairs, and communications while allowing states to retain autonomy in internal matters.
 
• Notable examples include the accession of Jammu and Kashmir to India on **October 26, 1947**, facilitated by the signing of the Instrument of Accession by Maharaja Hari Singh.
 
• This instrument played a crucial role in shaping the political boundaries of modern-day India and Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Independence Act 1947:**

 
 
• It marked the end of British rule in India and resulted in the creation of two dominions—India and Pakistan.
 
• Princely states were given the autonomy to decide their future—join India, Pakistan, or remain independent.
 
 
 
• **Standstill Agreement:**
 
 
• This agreement was signed between the dominions and princely states to maintain the status quo in administrative arrangements until a decision on accession was made.
 
• It provided temporary stability during the transitional phase post-independence.
 
 
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir Accession:**
 
 
• Maharaja Hari Singh of Jammu and Kashmir signed the Instrument of Accession with India during the 1947-1948 conflict.
 
• The decision was influenced by Pakistan-backed tribal invasions in the region.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lord Mountbatten:**
 
 
• As the last Viceroy of India, Lord Mountbatten played a key role in facilitating the accession of princely states to either dominion.
 
• He advised rulers on the strategic and practical implications of their decisions.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Instrument:**
 
 
• It laid the foundation for the integration of princely states into the Indian Union.
 
• The process was completed through additional measures like the States Reorganization Act, 1956.
